title: Identification of the interacting partners of a lysosomal membrane protein in living cells by BioID technique
protocol: Begin cell lysis with one 15-cm dish (or three 10-cm dishes) for each sample (HEK293T cells expressing BioID fusion protein or BioID constructs).
Change medium to fresh complete medium containing 50 μM biotin when cells reach 80% confluency.
Incubate cells for 16 h–18 h.
Collect the cells by removing medium completely by aspiration.
Collect the cells by pipetting with 10 ml/dish of PBS/EDTA into a 15 ml tube.
Wash the dish one more time with 5 mL PBS/EDTA to collect all residue cells.
Spin down for 5 min at 400 × g at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Discard the supernatant.
Wash the cells twice by spin down for 5 min at 400 × g at room temperature (20°C–25°C) with 10 mL/tube of PBS to remove all residue biotin.
Lysate the cells.
Resuspend the cells in 900 μL cell-suspension buffer.
Add 900 μL lysis buffer and pipette strongly but avoid making bubbles.
If hard to pipette due to DNA release, apply sonication at 30% amplitude for 15–30 s.
Add 180 μL of 20% Triton X-100 and mix by pipetting.
Keep the tubes on ice.
Position the sonicator probe tip in the sample just above the tube bottom to avoid making bubbles.
Sonicate samples for two sessions, each session for 30 s at 30% amplitude with a rest period of 2 min between sessions to prevent overheating.
Add 1.62 mL of prechilled 50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, and mix well.
Repeat one more session of sonication.
Aliquot the sample evenly into three prechilled 1.5-mL tubes.
Spin down the samples for 10 min at 16,500 × g, 4°C.
Carefully transfer all supernatant to a prechilled 5 mL tube.
Measure protein concentration using the DC protein assay kit with BSA as a standard.
Adjust the protein concentration of samples to match the lowest sample concentration with mix buffer.
Keep samples on ice until use.
Place three new 1.5-mL tubes in the Tamagawa magnetic stand.
Add 1 mL of mix buffer to each tube.
Mix stock of magnetic streptavidin beads well and add 150 μL of beads to each tube prepared previously.
Wait for 3 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Remove supernatant gently by pipette once the beads accumulate on one side of the tube wall.
Divide 1.2 mL of sample from step 14 to the three tubes containing equilibrated beads.
Resuspend the samples and beads with gentle pipetting.
Incubate the tube on a rotator at 4°C for overnight (at least 12 h).
Place the tubes on the magnetic stand and wait for 3 minutes to collect beads at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Remove the supernatant gently by pipetting, avoiding disturbing the beads attached to the tube walls.
Add 1.2 mL of wash buffer 1 to each tube and resuspend the beads gently by pipetting.
Rinse the beads with rotation in a rotator for 8 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Remove the supernatant carefully as described previously.
Pool beads from the same samples into one tube.
Add 1.2 mL of wash buffer 1 to one of the three tubes and resuspend gently.
Transfer resuspended sample from step 26 to the second of the three tubes, resuspending it gently.
Repeat this process to pool all beads from the same samples into a single tube in a final volume of 1.2 mL wash buffer 1.
Place the combined tube on a rotator for 8 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Wash once with 1.2 mL of wash buffer 2 as described previously.
Wash once with 1.2 mL of wash buffer 3 as described previously.
Wash once with 1.2 mL of 50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.4.
Remove the supernatant completely.
Add 110 μL Laemmli SDS sample buffer containing 2 mM biotin.
Save 10 μL of sample for further analysis by silver stain or western blot.
Use 100 μL of sample for mass spectrometric analysis.
If necessary, freeze the sample quickly in liquid nitrogen.
Frozen samples can be stored at -80°C until performing mass spectrometric analysis.
Prepare biological triplicate samples for reproducibility in mass spectrometric analysis.
Use a one-day-old gel to avoid modification by unreacted acrylamide.
Elute streptavidin bound proteins with 100 μL Laemmli SDS sample buffer containing 2 mM biotin at 98°C.
Concentrate the samples to 20 μL volume using a SpeedVac vacuum concentrator for 2 h at 25°C.
Load concentrated samples onto a polyacrylamide mini gel, ensuring distance between each sample to avoid cross-contamination.
Stop electrophoresis when the dye front migrates from the stacking gel to the separation gel.
Wash the gel three times with 200 mL of ultra-pure water using a shaker and discard the washing solution.
Stain the gel according to the CGP stain method for at least 1 h at 25°C.
Discard the staining solution and wash the gel three times with 200 mL ultra-pure water for 1 h to visualize protein bands.
Cut the visualized band into four pieces using a clean razor blade and transfer them to a 600 μL microcentrifuge tube.
Soak the gel pieces in 300 μL of de-staining buffer to de-stain CBB G-250.
Incubate for 30 min at 37°C and exchange the de-staining buffer until the gel pieces turn clear.
Dehydrate the gel pieces by adding 100% acetonitrile.
Exchange 100% acetonitrile until the gel pieces turn white.
Discard the acetonitrile and dry the gel pieces completely with a SpeedVac vacuum concentrator for 10 min at 25°C.
Add 50 μL of reducing buffer onto the dried gel pieces and incubate for 2 h at 37°C.
Add 50 μL of alkylating buffer onto the reduced gel pieces and incubate for 30 min at 25°C.
Remove the buffer after alkylation by pipetting.
Wash gel pieces three times with 200 μL of ultra-pure water for 10 min at 25°C.
Exchange washing solution with 200 μL of 100% acetonitrile and reswell with 200 μL of ultra-pure water.
This step is repeated three times.
Remove the washing solution and dehydrate the gel pieces with 100% acetonitrile.
Dry the gel pieces with a centrifugal vacuum concentrator for 10 min at 25°C.
Reswell the dried gels completely with 2 μL of 10 ng/μL TPCK-treated trypsin.
Add 30 μL of digestion buffer to cover the top of gel pieces.
Incubate samples for 12 hours at 37°C to digest with trypsin.
Store resulting peptides at 4°C for up to 1 week.
Pause point: Store peptide mixture at -20°C for one month if not immediately analyzed.
Transfer digested peptides mixture to vials in the LC autosampler.
Acidify the peptides solution by adding 1% formic acid.
Adjust all sample volumes to equal amounts.
Analyze digestion mixtures with a nanospray column (NTCC-360/75–3-105) using EASY-nLC 1200 coupled with a Q Exactive HF-X mass spectrometer.
Use a flow rate of 300 nL/min for LC-MS/MS analysis.
Separate peptides using a 50 min linear gradient from 0% to 64% B over 50 minutes.
Use solvent A (0.1% formic acid in water) and solvent B (0.1% formic acid in 80% acetonitrile) for separation.
Perform LC-MS/MS analysis according to the parameters listed in Table 1.
